rationale: Indie developers, agencies, and startups running LLM-dependent production services are a specific, nameable buyer who already pay for monitoring tools (PagerDuty, Better Uptime, Datadog) — the willingness-to-pay baseline exists. The service — polling major LLM API endpoints independently, detecting latency spikes and outages before status pages update, and alerting via webhook/email/Slack — is genuinely buildable with Claude + a lightweight polling script + a simple dashboard page + Stripe, and once live it runs fully automated with no per-customer human work. The HN thread with 64 upvotes and 70 comments confirms broad resonance among the exact target audience. Defensibility is modest (easily copied in principle), but speed-to-market and aggregated multi-provider historical latency data create growing lock-in.
solution_plan: The micro-service is an independent LLM API uptime and latency monitor — it polls OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Cohere, and others every 60 seconds and alerts subscribers before official status pages catch up. BUILD: the factory sets up a polling script (Claude + cron), a simple public status dashboard (static page or Vercel deploy), a Stripe subscription link ($19-49/mo tiers), and an intake form for webhook/email/Slack alert destinations — no coding by the operator, just configuration approvals. SELL: reach developers where they already are — post in HN (Show HN), tweet at the exact HN thread participants, post in relevant Discord/Slack communities (e.g. OpenAI developer Discord, Latent Space), and run a targeted LinkedIn post to 'AI startup CTO / indie developer' — outreach goes out only after operator approval. MAINTAIN: polling, alerting, billing, and basic support FAQs all run via Claude + code; the only recurring operator touch is approving new outreach batches and reviewing the weekly anomaly digest.
